voices.note: the mishna (41a), cited by lemma at 41b.3
the baraita taught in accordance with Rava, 41b.6-7

props.gloss_en: one may not slaughter into a hole [in the ground] at all
the mishna's further clause: but one may make a hole inside his house so that the blood will enter it
and in the marketplace one may not do so
Abaye: the first clause ('not into a hole at all') speaks of a hole in the marketplace
Rava: the mishna means -- not into a hole at all; one who wants to clean his courtyard makes a place outside the hole and slaughters, the blood running down into the hole
one may make a place outside the hole and slaughter there, the blood flowing down into the hole
[in the marketplace not] so that he not emulate the heretics
one travelling on a ship with no place to slaughter puts his hand outside the ship and slaughters, the blood running down the ship's sides
[in the marketplace not] because it is said 'and in their statutes you shall not walk' (Lev 18:3)
and if he did so [in the marketplace], he requires examination after him

supports.gloss_en: תניא כוותיה דרבא -- the baraita states the outside-the-hole procedure for one who would clean his courtyard, as Rava read the mishna

objections.gloss_en: והא אמרת אין שוחטין לגומא כלל? -- how may he make a hole in his house, if one may not slaughter into a hole at all? (Abaye first answered: the first clause is the marketplace -- refuted at 41b.4)

answered_by.gloss_en: אלא אמר רבא הכי קאמר: not into the hole itself at all; in the house one slaughters at a place outside the hole and the blood runs into it

objections.gloss_en: מדקתני סיפא ובשוק לא יעשה כן, מכלל דרישא לאו בשוק עסקינן -- the latter clause names the marketplace, so the first clause is not about it
